health_zone_table.basis: SitRep73 Tableau 2 (2026-07-26) transcribed and reconciled against the INSP PDF (14 pages, sha256 f24c52e66be84e43d0fd9a3dcfe3c02174a583b52188fd11228ca2d856e78128); page 2's Haut-Uele 38 typo is superseded by the page-4 detailed rows totaling 39.

reconciliation.note: SitRep73 is net-additive at the national boundary: 3200 + 62 = 3262 confirmed and 1405 + 32 = 1437 deaths. All detailed zone rows close to their province totals and the five corrected province totals close to 3262/1437. A minus-two death harmonization is declared in Nord-Kivu and appears in Katwa's day column, so the net +32 reconciles mathematically but is not a pure incident-death count. The page-2 Haut-Uele confirmed total of 38 is a source typo: its five detailed rows total 39 and the corrected province vector closes to the headline.

lab_indicators_24h.note: National aggregate over the four provincial laboratory paragraphs: Ituri 186 analysed / 53 positive (39 living, 14 deaths) = 28.4%; Nord-Kivu 113/8 (5 living, 3 deaths) = 7.0%; Haut-Uele 8/1 (death) = 12.5%; Tshopo 5/0. The 62 positives equal the notified 62 confirmations. Apparent national positivity is 62/312 = 19.9%, down from 33.3% at SR72 on analysed volume 372 -> 312; one cycle is not a settled force-of-infection trend.

care_continuity: SitRep73 reports 723 patients in isolation (325 confirmed / 398 suspected) at 76.8% national occupancy; Ituri 531/800 = 66.4%, while Nord-Kivu worsened to 192/141 = 136.2%.
The bed identity closes exactly: 681 at J-1 plus 126 admissions minus 84 exits equals the 723 end-of-day census.
Only 2 of 30 North Kivu ambulances were reported functional, and only 4 of 11 hotspot health zones submitted logistics data.
Only 175 of 1170 triage units were reported functional, while frontline burden totals 134 confirmed and 40 deaths across Ituri and North Kivu.
The SitRep explicitly states that continuity of essential health services is compromised, increasing indirect non-Ebola mortality.
highlights: No new health zone was affected; the footprint remains 48 of 140 zones across five provinces, with 47 in active transmission.
National 3262/1437 closes from the detailed zone table after correcting page 2's Haut-Uele 38 typo to the detailed-table value 39.
The source declares a minus-two Nord-Kivu death harmonization. National deaths move 1405 + 32 = 1437, but the +32 is a net notification/reclassification value rather than a pure incident-death count.
Tshopo contact follow-up is unavailable in the table of record; the adjacent 90.9% prose is stale carry-forward and is not promoted.
North Kivu treatment capacity worsened from 171/141 (121.3%) to 192/141 (136.2%) even as national isolation fell from 773 to 723.
Laboratory positivity fell to 19.9% (62/312) from 33.3% (124/372), with all 62 provincial positives reconciling to the notified +62 confirmations.
Ituri reports 123 frontline infections/37 deaths and North Kivu 11/3, producing 134 confirmed and 40 deaths nationally.

alerts_total.data_gap_note: SitRep73 Tableau 3: Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uele report; Tshopo and Sud-Kivu are ND. Reporting rows close exactly to 1303 alerts, 1078 investigated, 216 validated living and 110 validated deaths, with 216+110=326 suspects. National investigation is 82.7%. Missing provinces are not coerced to zero.

challenges.finding: Reluctance toward post-mortem sampling, community resistance and insecurity targeting burial teams delay confirmation, under-estimate cases and disrupt response activities.
challenges.response: Intensify RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams and increase burial-team capacity.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of providers and strikes in Bunia and Rwampara interrupt response activities including safe and dignified burials.
challenges.response: Regularise provider payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: CTE/CT capacity is insufficient: 136.2% occupancy in Nord-Kivu and 66.4% in Ituri, causing admission delays and raising nosocomial-transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact follow-up remains weak: Ituri 75.6%, Nord-Kivu 85.2% and Haut-Uele 60.0%, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays; reinforce supervision and stabilise reporting completeness.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and pre-positioning at control points delay transfer and isolation.
challenges.response: Pre-position ambulances including at PoE/PoC and deploy treatment capacity by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient essential medicines and medical inputs weaken holistic case management.
challenges.response: Urgently procure and distribute essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs and only 175 of 1170 triage units functional raise nosocomial risk; Ituri reports 123 frontline infections/37 deaths and Nord-Kivu 11/3.
challenges.response: Urgently procure IPC supplies and reinforce IPC training.

challenges.finding: Extension to Haut-Uele and Tshopo alongside high mobility raises urban, riverine and cross-border spread risk.
challenges.response: Activate priority PoE/PoC and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Proximity laboratories at Butembo and Mambasa are not yet installed, prolonging confirmation delays and allowing transmission to remain undetected.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across response pillars.
challenges.response: Mobilise resources urgently and advocate with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access linked to CODECO and ADF restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential health services is compromised, raising indirect non-Ebola mortality.
challenges.response: Implement free care effectively and reinforce continuity of essential health services.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: SitRep73 Tableau 4: 15498 contacts under follow-up and 12122 seen = 78.2%. Ituri remains computed only over reporting health zones; Damas, Fataki, Kilo, Kambala, Logo, Mambasa, Nyankunde and Rimba are unavailable. Tshopo is ND in the table; adjacent prose repeats SR72's 90.9%, treated as stale carry-forward and not promoted. Sud-Kivu follow-up is closed (0/0, NA).

patient_movement_total.data_gap_note: SitRep73 Tableau 6: 723 in isolation at end of day (325 confirmed / 398 suspected) at 76.8% national occupancy over 941 reported beds. Ituri 531/800 = 66.4%; Nord-Kivu 192/141 = 136.2%; Haut-Uele and Tshopo ND. The bed identity closes: 681 + 126 - 84 = 723. Exits are 14 deaths + 57 non-cases + 12 recovered + 1 escape + 0 transfers = 84.

priorities.priority: Relieve North Kivu's 136.2% occupancy immediately; its census rose 171 -> 192 with bed capacity fixed at 141 while national isolation fell.
Restore North Kivu transport and reporting: only 2 of 30 ambulances were functional and only 4 of 11 hotspot zones submitted logistics data.
Raise follow-up from 78.2% toward the 95% threshold and restore missing Ituri zone reporting; treat Tshopo as unavailable, not 90.9%.
Restore triage and household decontamination: only 175/1170 triage units were functional and 45/94 case households were decontaminated within 48 hours.
Protect the 134 infected frontline workers/40 deaths reported across Ituri and North Kivu with IPC supplies, training and functional triage.
Fund continuity of essential services alongside outbreak response because the SitRep explicitly reports compromised services and indirect mortality risk.

preserved_conflicts: SitRep73 national headline is DRC-only (3262 confirmed / 1437 deaths); the country-scope snapshot adds Uganda 20/2/11 separately -> 3282 confirmed / 1439 deaths / 594 recovered.

PAGE-2 HAUT-UELE TYPO: Tableau 1 prints 38 confirmed, but page 1/2 narrative says 39 and Tableau 2's five detailed rows sum 7+12+8+1+11=39. The corrected province vector closes exactly to the 3262 headline; Haut-Uele 39 is promoted and the printed 38 is preserved as a source conflict.

TSHOPO CONTACT CONFLICT: Tableau 4 records Tshopo as ND while adjacent prose repeats 90.9% from SR72; page 12 gives no current Tshopo percentage. Tshopo is unavailable/unscoreable at SR73, not carried forward.

NORD-KIVU DEATH HARMONIZATION: the source declares minus two deaths, represented as -2 community deaths at Katwa. The national boundary closes 1405 + 32 = 1437, but the net +32 must not be read as 32 newly occurring deaths.

STALE ZONE CFR CELLS: Tableau 2 prints stale CFRs for Beni (69.8% on 44/34), Kalunguta (75.0% on 5/3) and Drodro (66.7% on 10/5). Count-derived values are 77.3%, 60.0% and 50.0%; counts are promoted and the printed percentages preserved here.
The page-7 narrative calls the national alert movement an improvement, but investigation falls from 85.1% to 82.7%; the printed table values are promoted.
The PoE narrative for Nord-Kivu ends without numeric completeness/promptness values. No missing values are inferred.

review_notes: SitRep #073 (report date 2026-07-26; PDF cover publication date 2026-07-27; INSP WordPress post 25215/media 25216 published 2026-07-28). PDF sha256 f24c52e66be84e43d0fd9a3dcfe3c02174a583b52188fd11228ca2d856e78128, 1373025 bytes, 14 pages, independently re-fetched and hash-matched before extraction.
All 14 pages were rendered and visually inspected. They are present, ordered, nonblank and legible with no clipping, overlap, missing panels, broken glyphs, black boxes or rotation defects.

National 3262/1437 is supported by the page-1 headline and the detailed zone table. Page 2 incorrectly prints Haut-Uele 38; the page-4 zone rows sum to 39 and all province totals then close exactly to 3262. Haut-Uele 39 is promoted and the page-2 typo is preserved as a conflict.

The boundary is net-additive: 3200 + 62 = 3262 and 1405 + 32 = 1437. The source declares a minus-two Nord-Kivu death harmonization, represented in Katwa's day column; the net reported death increment reconciles but is not interpreted as 32 newly occurring deaths.

Tshopo contact follow-up is unavailable. The page-7 table prints ND while adjacent prose repeats 90.9% from SR72 and page 12 provides no current Tshopo value. The table-of-record wins; missingness is preserved rather than carried forward or coerced to zero.

Isolation reconciles exactly: 681 at J-1 + 126 admissions - 84 exits = 723 end-of-day; 325 confirmed + 398 suspected = 723. Nord-Kivu worsened to 192/141 = 136.2% while national occupancy fell to 76.8%.
Laboratory rows reconcile exactly to the notified +62: Ituri 53 + Nord-Kivu 8 + Haut-Uele 1 + Tshopo 0 = 62. National apparent positivity is 62/312 = 19.9%.
